details:
While I'm really stoked to see full-finger tracking on the index controllers, I can't help but feel some concern for finger positioning when it comes to gesture overrides. If I read the blog post correctly, then Index users will have the ability to toggle on and off the gesture overrides with a click of the joystick, while the game still tracks their fingers regardless of whether they're enabled or not. My main concern is how this would interact and feel on an avatar that needs to use an override for a different finger position, cause there are a limited amount of override slots after all.

Until a more robust solution can be found, I think a good option is to include a setting that toggles a legacy override system. Turning on this option would replace the Index's new gesture override system with the legacy one, but users can still click the joystick to toggle their full-finger tracking. The new gesture system would still be enabled by default, but it would give long-time users—and also new ones—the choice of whether they want full-finger fidelity on their animations or the override's intended finger positions.

For example, I know a few of my avatars use the HandGun override to play a punch animation since the more similar poses (RocknRoll and Fist) are already mapped to other overrides. Since the hand curls up into a fist, it feels correct to punch that way despite using the HandGun override. If somebody uses that same animation on Index controllers, they'll be punching with their fingers outstretched, which, when all you can see are your virtual hands, won't feel right. It's only one example, but moments like this can just as easily ruin immersion and avatar fidelity.

Similar to how the Vive Advanced Movement option became a toggleable setting, I can imagine an option like this being used in almost the same way.

tl;dr Adding a setting that toggles between the Index's new gesture override system and a legacy one.
title: Setting to toggle legacy finger overrides on Index controllers
